In the weeks leading up to Feb. 28, he argued against the operation in meetings in the Oval Office and Situation Room, at times to Mr. Trump’s considerable irritation, according to officials who discussed the matter with the president. But once Mr. Trump made up his mind, Mr. Vance defended the decision in public, including during tense television interviews. 万斯对战争的反对在白宫内部并非秘密。据与总统讨论过此事的官员透露，在2月28日之前的几周里，他在椭圆形办公室和战情室的会议上公开反对该行动，有时这让特朗普相当恼火。然而一旦特朗普做出决定，万斯就在公开场合为该决定辩护，包括在气氛紧张的电视采访中。 The vice president also became the public face of the peace effort, running a series of talks that yielded a memorandum of understanding in June. Its 60-day window closed in August with no agreement and with the two sides seemingly further apart than when the negotiations started. 副总统还成为了和平斡旋的代言人，主持了一系列谈判，并在6月达成了一项谅解备忘录。该备忘录在60天窗口期于8月结束时未促成任何协议，双方的分歧似乎比谈判开始时更大。 Mr. Trump had not seriously contemplated the war lasting long enough to strain U.S. stockpiles. He was fresh off the success of the quick military strike to capture Venezuela’s leader, and was impressed by how the United States and Israel had combined to attack Iranian nuclear sites over 12 days the previous year. Before launching the war in Iran, he had privately expected the government there to collapse within days. 特朗普此前并未认真思考过战争会持续到使美军库存面临压力的情况。他刚经历了快速突袭抓获委内瑞拉领导人的成功，也对前一年美以联合在12天内打击伊朗核设施的成果印象深刻。在对伊朗开战前，他私下里曾预计该国政府将在几天内崩溃。 As Mr. Vance was making his calls, the fighting ran well past the roughly six-week window that Pentagon planners had initially budgeted for the campaign. Senior White House advisers beyond the vice president did not believe they had a clear-enough understanding of how much the strikes had changed the calculus of the government in Tehran. 五角大楼规划者最初预设战斗会持续六周，在万斯致电指挥官时早已超过这个时限。除副总统外的白宫高级顾问们认为，他们对于打击在多大程度上改变了德黑兰政府的考量缺乏足够清晰的了解。 As the war dragged on, commanders were ordered to transfer more of their munitions. They watched with alarm as their stockpiles dwindled. 随着战争拖延，指挥官们接到命令调运更多弹药。看着自己的库存不断缩减，他们感到担忧。 By April, Mr. Trump could see the war was not going the way he had hoped. He authorized his team — including Mr. Vance, the president’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and the special envoy Steve Witkoff — to begin seeking a framework and negotiating a deal with Iran to end the conflict, an agreement that would leave the country’s authoritarians in control. The officials briefed on the calls with the commanders could not say what role, if any, the vice president’s findings played in the president’s shift toward diplomacy. 到了4月，特朗普已经看出战争并未朝着他所希望的方向发展。他授权自己的团队——包括万斯、总统女婿贾里德·库什纳以及特使史蒂夫·威特科夫——开始寻求建立一个框架，并与伊朗协商停火，而该协议将允许该国的威权统治者继续掌权。至于副总统的调研发现在总统转向外交的过程中发挥了何种作用，或是否发挥了作用，了解通话内容的官员无法给出回答。 Mr. Vance has developed a reputation inside the Trump administration for steeping himself in operational detail, a habit that some officials admire and others regard as too much in the weeds. Where Mr. Trump works in a way that leaves even his aides guessing how he arrives at decisions, Mr. Vance obsessively tracks the daily minutiae, including military operations, the internal dynamics of the Iranian political system and the sourcing of intelligence assessments. 万斯在特朗普政府内部树立了喜欢深究具体执行细节的声誉，这种习惯让部分官员颇为赞赏，但也被一些人认为过多关注旁枝末节。相比之下，特朗普的工作方式甚至让他的助手都无法猜透他是如何做出决定的，而万斯则执着于跟进日常的琐碎事务，包括军事行动、伊朗政治体制的内部动态以及情报评估的来源。 本月早些时候，萨缪尔·帕帕罗将军在加拿大参加一场防务官员会议。 John Ratcliffe, the C.I.A. director, has given him direct access to agency analysts; Mr. Vance knows some of them by first name and calls their desks to ask about raw intelligence or items in his morning briefing, intelligence officials said. 情报官员表示，中央情报局局长约翰·拉特克利夫给予了他直接联系该局分析师的权限；万斯能叫出其中一些人的名字，并会直接打电话到他们的办公桌询问原始情报或早间简报中的内容。 But such access is the exception. For most senior officials, information about the war remains hard to come by. 但这种权限只是例外。对于大多数高级官员而言，关于这场战争的信息依然难以获取。 Adam Goldman对本文有报道贡献。 Jonathan Swan 是时报白宫记者，报道特朗普政府新闻。可以通过Signal安全地联系他： @jonathan.941 Adam Entous 是《纽约时报》驻华盛顿调查记者，主要关注国家安全和情报事务。 Maggie Haberman 是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

items.title: 美国在阿富汗的“永久战争”：25年影像全记录
items.description: 《纽约时报》2026年9月11日 Jim Huylebroek for The New York Times America’s “forever war” in Afghanistan began only weeks after the Sept. 11 attacks and lasted just short of 20 years, ending in the chaos of Aug. 15, 2021, when the capital, Kabul, fell once again to the Taliban. 美国在阿富汗的“永久战争”始于9·11袭击仅数周后，持续近20年，最终在2021年8月15日的混乱中结束——首都喀布尔再次落入塔利班之手。 Journalists for The New York Times covered the war from beginning to end and have continued capturing the lives of Afghanistan’s people as they navigate a scarred landscape and an uncertain future. 《纽约时报》的记者从头到尾报道了这场战争，并继续记录阿富汗人民的生活。他们穿行于伤痕累累的土地，面对不确定的未来。 2001-2002 2001-2002 The War Begins 战争开始 Operation Enduring Freedom began on Oct. 7, 2001, with an American bombing campaign against Al Qaeda and the Taliban. American Special Operations forces teams linked up with Afghan militias opposed to the Taliban, mainly the Northern Alliance, to drive the Taliban from power. Kabul fell in mid-November, along with the Taliban stronghold of Kandahar. “持久自由行动”于2001年10月7日开始，美国对基地组织和塔利班发动轰炸。美国特种作战部队与反对塔利班的阿富汗民兵——主要是北方联盟——联手，意图将塔利班赶下台。喀布尔于11月中旬陷落，塔利班据点坎大哈也一并陷落。 In December, Osama bin Laden, Al Qaeda’s leader, escaped to Pakistan through the mountains around Tora Bora. That same month, an interim Afghan government led by Hamid Karzai was installed. 12月，基地组织领导人奥萨马·本·拉登穿过托拉博拉周边山区逃往巴基斯坦。同月，由哈米德·卡尔扎伊领导的阿富汗临时政府成立。 James Hill for The New York Times Northern Alliance troops firing on Taliban positions in rugged territory outside the northeastern city of Taloqan in October 2001. 2001年10月，北方联盟部队在东北部城市塔洛坎外围的崎岖地带向塔利班阵地开火。 Fighters for the Northern Alliance heading to the front lines near the besieged Taliban stronghold of Kunduz in November 2001. 2001年11月，北方联盟的战士前往被围困的塔利班据点昆都士附近的前线。 Tyler Hicks/The New York Times On their way into Kabul in November 2001, Northern Alliance members found a Taliban fighter in a ditch and killed him, despite his pleas. 2001年11月，北方联盟成员在进军喀布尔途中发现一名塔利班武装分子藏身沟渠，尽管对方苦苦哀求，北方联盟成员仍将其杀害。 An American B-52 bomber circling above Tora Bora in eastern Afghanistan in December 2001. 2001年12月，一架美国B-52轰炸机在阿富汗东部托拉博拉上空盘旋。 Joao Silva for The New York Times Fighters for the Eastern Alliance, another anti-Taliban militia, running for cover from Al Qaeda sniper fire in the Tora Bora mountains in December 2001. 2001年12月，另一支反塔利班民兵组织东部联盟的战士在托拉博拉山区躲避基地组织狙击手的火力。 2003-2007 2003-2007 Drift to Iraq 转向伊拉克 Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld announced an end to major combat operations in Afghanistan in May 2003. Even with a major reconstruction effort underway there, and about 8,000 American troops in place, President George W. Bush’s administration began shifting combat resources to the war in Iraq. 国防部长唐纳德·拉姆斯菲尔德于2003年5月宣布阿富汗主要作战行动结束。尽管那里正在进行大规模重建，并且约有8000名美军驻扎，乔治·W·布什政府已开始将作战资源转向伊拉克战争。American soldiers from the 10th Mountain Division yelling to others to get out of the line of fire after being ambushed by Taliban fighters in southern Afghanistan in June 2006. 2006年6月，在阿富汗南部遭到塔利班战士伏击后，美国第10山地师的士兵大声呼喊其他人离开火力线。 Tyler Hicks/The New York Times Women in Kabul waiting to vote in October 2004. Afghanistan’s landmark presidential election quickly fell into dispute. 2004年10月，喀布尔的妇女排队等待投票。阿富汗具有里程碑意义的总统选举很快陷入争议。 Mohammad Akbar holding the hand of his nephew, Mohammad, age 3, at a hospital in Kandahar in May 2006. The boy was injured in an attack by U.S. forces and suffered burn injuries. 2006年5月，穆罕默德·阿克巴在坎大哈一家医院握着三岁侄子穆罕默德的手。这名男孩在美国部队的一次袭击中受伤，遭受烧伤。 Joao Silva for The New York Times British soldiers of the Royal Anglians B Company, part of NATO forces, firing toward Taliban positions after coming under attack during a patrol in Kajaki in July 2007. 2007年7月，作为北约部队一部分的英国皇家安格利亚团B连士兵在卡贾基巡逻时遭到袭击，向塔利班阵地开火。 Wounded soldiers in the Korengal Valley in eastern Afghanistan in October 2007. 2007年10月，阿富汗东部科伦加尔山谷中受伤的士兵。 Tyler Hicks/The New York Times Afghan National Army soldiers detained a man whom they believed to be a Taliban fighter during the search of a village in southern Afghanistan in May 2006. 2006年5月，阿富汗国民军士兵在阿富汗南部搜查一个村庄时，拘留了一名他们认为是塔利班战士的男子。 2008-2010 2008-2010 Recommitment and Surge 重新承诺与增兵 In February 2009, the new American president, Barack Obama, declared a recommitment to the war and deployed 17,000 more troops to Afghanistan, adding to the 36,000 already there. 2009年2月，新任美国总统贝拉克·奥巴马宣布重新投入于这场战争，并An Army patrol worked its way through the Korengal Valley in April 2009 to meet with a group of village elders. An I.E.D. exploded. Then the Taliban attacked. Soldiers scrambled. One died. 2009年4月，一支陆军巡逻队穿过科伦加尔山谷，准备与一群村中长老会面。一枚简易爆炸装置爆炸。随后塔利班发动袭击。士兵们仓皇应对。一人死亡。 Moises Saman for The New York Times A German soldier burning a flare at a campsite in the desert of Kunduz Province, in October 2009. 2009年10月，一名德国士兵在昆都士省沙漠中的一个营地点燃信号弹。 A suicide bomber struck near a hotel in Kabul in December 2009, killing at least eight people and wounding dozens. 2009年12月，一名自杀式炸弹袭击者在喀布尔一家酒店附近发动袭击，造成至少八人死亡、数十人受伤。 Moises Saman for The New York Times A bullet-pierced window at a Kabul guesthouse attacked by the Taliban in November 2009. Five United Nations workers were killed. 2009年11月，喀布尔一家宾馆遭到塔利班袭击，窗户被子弹击穿。五名联合国工作人员遇害。 Marines came under attack in Marja, in Helmand Province, in February 2010 while on their way to check a building that had been bombed earlier in the day. Most of the Marines were experiencing combat for the first time. 2010年2月，海军陆战队员在赫尔曼德省马尔贾遭到袭击，当时他们正前往检查一座当天早些时候被轰炸的建筑。大多数海军陆战队员是首次经历实战。 Moises Saman for The New York Times Village elders meeting in Marja in March 2010. 2010年3月，村中长老在马尔贾开会。 Afghan soldiers rushing a wounded police officer to an American helicopter in Kunar Province in March 2010. 2010年3月，库纳尔省，阿富汗士兵将一名受伤的警察紧急送往一架美国直升机。 Damon Winter/The New York Times American soldiers on a transport plane about to land in Mazar-i-Sharif in April 2010. 2010年4月，一架即将降落在马扎里沙里夫的运输机上的美国士兵。 An Afghan man who was detained on suspicion of being involved in an attack by militants on the first day of a national peace council meeting in Kabul in June 2010. 2010年6月，一名涉嫌参与武装分子在喀布尔全国和平委员会会议首日的袭击而被拘留的阿富汗男子。 Damon Winter/The New York Times Members of the First Battalion, 87th Infantry, tending to a wounded comrade in Kunduz in September 2010. 2010年9月，第87步兵团第一营的成员在昆都士照料一名受伤的战友。 2011-2013 2011-2013 A Troop Drawdown 部队撤减 In May 2011, a U.S. Navy SEAL team killed Osama bin Laden in a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan, where he had been living for years. In June, Mr. Obama announced that he would pull 33,000 troops from Afghanistan by mid-2012. 2011年5月，一支美国海军海豹突击队击毙奥萨马·本·拉登，地点在巴基斯坦阿伯塔巴德的一处院落，他已在那里居住多年。6月，奥巴马宣布，他将在2012年中期前从阿富汗撤出3.3万名军人。Soldiers boarding a transport helicopter in Kunduz in March 2011. 2011年3月，士兵们在昆都士登上一架运输直升机。 Andrea Bruce for The New York Times The mother of Khan Mohammad, a 3-month-old baby who died from exposure to the cold, being comforted before her child was washed and buried in the Nasaji Bagrami Camp for displaced persons in Kabul in February 2012. 2012年2月，在喀布尔的纳萨吉·巴格拉米流离失所者营地，三个月大的婴儿汗·穆罕默德因受寒而亡。他的母亲在为孩子清洗遗体并下葬前接受安慰。 Afghan soldiers, left, and American soldiers blew up a Taliban firing position in the village of Layadira, in Kandahar Province, in February 2013. 2013年2月，阿富汗士兵（左）和美国士兵在坎大哈省拉亚迪拉村炸毁一个塔利班射击阵地。 Sergey Ponomarev for The New York Times Members of the 101st Airborne Division in Paktia Province in April 2013. 2013年4月，第101空降师的成员在帕克蒂亚省。 Samiullah, 8 months old and malnourished, being held by his mother, Islam Bibi, 15, at a hospital in Lashkar Gah, in Helmand Province, in September 2013. 2013年9月，在赫尔曼德省拉什卡尔加一家医院，15岁的母亲伊斯兰·比比怀抱着八个月大、营养不良的萨米乌拉。 Daniel Berehulak for The New York Times Sayed Wazir, 40, a former mujahedeen, firing a rocket toward Taliban positions in Wardak Province in November 2013. 2013年11月，40岁的前圣战者赛义德·瓦齐尔在瓦尔达克省向塔利班阵地发射火箭弹。 The view from a Humvee of Highway 1, which links Kabul with Afghanistan’s other major cities, in November 2013. 2013年11月，从悍马车上眺望连接喀布尔与阿富汗其他主要城市的一号高速公路。 2014-2018 2014-2018 A Taliban Resurgence 塔利班卷土重来 On Dec. 31, 2014, the combat mission in Afghanistan formally ended, but the American military presence in the country did not. Mr. Obama announced a timetable for the withdrawal of most troops by the end of 2016. 2014年12月31日，阿富汗的战斗任务正式结束，但美国在该国的军事存在并未结束。奥巴马宣布了在2016年底前撤出大部分军队的时间表。 After a 2014 election marred by fraud, Ashraf Ghani became president, but signed a power-sharing agreement with his top opponent, Abdullah Abdullah. 在2014年一场因舞弊而备受诟病的选举后，阿什拉夫·加尼成为总统，但与他的主要对手阿卜杜拉·阿卜杜拉签署了权力分享协议。 On the battlefield, the Afghan security forces increasingly struggled against the Taliban, taking heavy casualties and losing territory. 在战场上，阿富汗安全部队日益难以对抗塔利班，承受重大伤亡并丢失领土。 In August 2017, President Trump, early in his first term in office, said he would continue to prosecute the war. 2017年8月，特朗普总统在其第一个任期初期表示，他将继续推进这场战争。 Bryan Denton for The New York Times An Afghan police officer, Mohammad Qassim, 28, recovering at a hospital run by Emergency, an Italian nonprofit group, after losing his right leg to a Taliban explosive in Marja, Helmand Province. 在赫尔曼德省马尔贾，28岁的阿富汗警察穆罕默德·卡西姆在意大利非营利组织“急诊”运营的医院中康复，他因塔利班的爆炸物失去了右腿。 The aftermath of a U.S. airstrike that hit a Doctors Without Borders hospital in Kunduz in October 2015. Forty-two people were killed in the attack. 2015年10月，美国空袭击中昆都士一家无国界医生医院后的景象。42人在袭击中丧生。 Jim Huylebroek for The New York Times The bodies of 20 commandos lined up in November 2018 outside the governor’s office in Sang-e-Masha, in Ghazni Province. Their company was almost destroyed fighting the Taliban. 2018年11月，加兹尼省桑格-马沙省长办公室外，20名突击队员的遗体排成一列。他们的连队在对抗塔利班时几乎被摧毁。 A view of the outskirts of Lashkar Gah in Helmand Province in March 2016. 2016年3月，赫尔曼德省拉什卡尔加郊区的景象。 Adam Ferguson for The New York Times The Kart-e-Sakhi cemetery in Kabul in April 2016. 2016年4月，喀布尔的卡尔特萨希公墓。 2018-2020 2018-2020 A Deal With the Taliban 与塔利班达成协议 In late 2018, American and Taliban negotiators began holding peace talks in Doha, Qatar. The Afghan government was excluded from the talks; the Taliban refused to meet with its officials. 2018年底，美国和塔利班谈判代表开始在卡塔尔多哈举行和平谈判。阿富汗政府被排除在谈判之外；塔利班拒绝与其官员会面。 On Feb. 29, 2020, the United States signed a peace deal with the Taliban, opening the door to a gradual, final troop withdrawal from Afghanistan and the beginning of direct talks between the Afghan government and the Taliban to determine the country’s future. 2020年2月29日，美国与塔利班签署和平协议，为从阿富汗逐步撤军打开大门，并开启阿富汗政府与塔利班之间的直接谈判，以决定该国的未来。A funeral for one of 63 people killed at a wedding in Kabul by an Islamic State suicide bomber in August 2019. 2019年8月，一名伊斯兰国自杀式炸弹袭击者在喀布尔一场婚礼上制造爆炸，造成63人遇难，图为其中一名遇难者的葬礼。 Jim Huylebroek for The New York Times A crater left by a car-bomb attack in Kabul in September 2019. The Taliban claimed responsibility. 2019年9月，喀布尔汽车炸弹袭击留下的弹坑。塔利班声称对此负责。 Afghan police officers inspecting a replacement trench after their base was overrun by the Taliban in February 2020. 2020年2月，阿富汗警察在其基地被塔利班攻占后检查一条新建的战壕。 Jim Huylebroek for The New York Times Two children passing members of a Taliban Red Unit, an elite force, in the Alingar district of Laghman in March 2020. 2020年3月，两名儿童在拉格曼省阿林加区经过塔利班精锐部队“红色部队”成员身旁。 2021-2026 2021-2026 The Taliban’s Return 塔利班回归 On April 14, 2021, the recently sworn-in U.S. president, Joseph R. Biden Jr., called for a complete withdrawal of all American forces from Afghanistan by Sept. 11, 2021. 2021年4月14日，刚刚宣誓就职的美国总统小约瑟夫·R·拜登呼吁在2021年9月11日前从阿富汗完全撤出所有美军。 The United States had spent about $2 trillion on the war effort. About 2,400 American troops and nearly 700 troops from other nations in the coalition died. More than 40,000 civilians were killed, as well as an estimated 60,000 Afghan security forces. 美国在这场战争中花费了约2万亿美元。约2400名美军和近700名来自联军其他国家的军人死亡。超过4万名平民被杀，另有估计达6万名阿富汗安全部队人员死亡。 After the rushed withdrawal of U.S. forces, the Afghan government did not mount a significant resistance, and Taliban forces quickly regained control. Many Afghans feared a return to civil war between the Taliban and the remaining anti-Taliban fighters, but the violence affecting civilians dropped sharply with the end of the U.S. war. 在美军匆忙撤离后，阿富汗政府没有组织有效的抵抗，塔利班部队迅速重新控制局势。许多阿富汗人担心塔利班与剩余反塔利班战士之间再次爆发内战，但随着美国战争的结束，影响平民的暴力事件急剧下降。 In 2022, the Taliban government imposed a series of edicts governing every aspect of daily life, which remain in place. The rules are particularly strict for women and girls, who are no longer allowed to work at most jobs or seek formal education beyond sixth grade. 2022年，塔利班政府颁布了一系列管理日常生活各个方面的法令，这些法令仍然有效。这些规定对妇女和女孩尤其严格，她们不再被允许从事大多数工作或寻求六年级以上的正规教育。 Military conflict has not disappeared. In late 2025, Pakistan began a campaign against the armed groups operating on its border with Afghanistan, while the Taliban tighten their grip on Afghan society and defend their rule against the few remaining forces of resistance. 军事冲突并未消失。2025年底，巴基斯坦开始对在其与阿富汗边境活动的武装团体发起行动，同时塔利班收紧对阿富汗社会的控制，并抵御少数残余抵抗力量以捍卫其统治。 An American soldier aboard a Chinook helicopter as U.S. troops began their withdrawal from the country, loading up ammunition and supplies from Kandahar Airfield in May 2021. 2021年5月，美国军队开始从阿富汗撤军，一名美国士兵在坎大哈机场的一架支奴干直升机上装载弹药和补给。 Tyler Hicks/The New York Times A passenger in a car awaiting clearance at a security checkpoint in Herat in July 2021. The Taliban would soon seize Herat, the country’s third-largest city. 2021年7月，赫拉特一个安全检查站，一名车内乘客等待放行。塔利班很快将夺取该国第三大城市赫拉特。 On the day that Afghanistan’s capital, Kabul, fell to the Taliban, the group’s fighters rode a Humvee near a roundabout in the city on Aug. 15, 2021. The date is now celebrated in Afghanistan as the moment of the country’s liberation from U.S. occupation. 2021年8月15日，阿富汗首都喀布尔落入塔利班之手当天，该组织战士乘坐一辆悍马车经过城中一个环岛。这一天现在在阿富汗被视为庆祝国家从美国占领下解放的时刻。 Jim Huylebroek for The New York Times With the U.S. withdrawal deadline looming, mayhem persisted outside the Kabul airport as American Marines stood guard in August 2021. Even some Afghans holding special immigrant visas were turned away to give priority to U.S. citizens. 2021年8月，随着美国撤军期限临近，喀布尔机场外混乱持续，美国海军陆战队员站岗守卫。甚至一些持有特殊移民签证的阿富汗人也因美国优先处理本国公民而被拒之门外。 In August 2021, during the last days of the U.S. evacuation, there was another spasm of violence, when a suicide bomb exploded outside the gates of the crowded airport in Kabul. An Islamic State affiliate claimed responsibility for the attack, which killed 13 U.S. service members and scores of civilians. 2021年8月，在美国撤离的最后几天，又发生了暴力事件，一枚自杀式炸弹在拥挤的喀布尔机场门外爆炸。一个与伊斯兰国有关联的组织声称负责，袭击造成13名美国军人和数十名平民死亡。 Victor J. Blue for The New York Times Before the city fell, Khalil Haqqani appeared at a mosque in Kabul to help establish Taliban authority. When the Taliban declared an interim government, they appointed many loyalists from their rule in the 1990s, including Mr. Haqqani. 在城市陷落前，哈利勒·哈卡尼出现在喀布尔一座清真寺，帮助建立塔利班权威。当塔利班宣布临时政府时，他们任命了许多20世纪90年代统治时期的效忠者，包括哈卡尼在内。 Relatives and neighbors at the site of a U.S. drone strike that killed 10 civilians in Kabul in August 2021. 2021年8月，喀布尔一次美国无人机袭击造成10名平民死亡，图为亲属和邻居在袭击现场。 David Guttenfelder for The New York Times Children flying homemade kites on a hillside graveyard in Kabul in December 2021. The first Taliban government had banned kite flying, and Afghans feared that the pastime and other activities would be outlawed again. 2021年12月，儿童在喀布尔一个山坡坟场放自制风筝。塔利班第一届政府曾禁止放风筝，阿富汗人担心这种消遣和其他活动会再次被禁止。 A math class in a secret classroom in Afghanistan in May 2026. The Taliban banned formal education beyond sixth grade for girls. 2026年5月，阿富汗一间秘密教室里的数学课。塔利班禁止女孩接受六年级以上的正规教育。 Elise Blanchard for The New York Times Afghan women and children who had just arrived from Pakistan waiting to be registered as returnees at the Torkham border crossing in Nangarhar Province in October 2023. Seven families paid to travel with their belongings from Pakistan. 2023年10月，刚刚从巴基斯坦抵达的阿富汗妇女和儿童在楠格哈尔省托尔哈姆边境口岸等待被登记为回乡人员。七个家庭自费携带家当从巴基斯坦辗转而来。 Nasiba Ameni, 30, holding her son Abdul Hamad, 1, at a malnutrition ward in Olqan Hospital, in Daykundi Province, in December 2025. Abdul has a heart disease, and his recovery is complicated by severe malnutrition. 2025年12月，30岁的纳西巴·阿梅尼在代孔迪省奥尔坎医院营养不良病房抱着一岁的儿子阿卜杜勒·哈马德。阿卜杜勒患有心脏病，他的康复因严重营养不良而变得棘手。 Tomas Munita for The New York Times Visiting the remains of a house in August 2026 that was damaged during Pakistani airstrikes two months earlier in the village of Mandakhel, in Paktia Province. 2026年8月，探访帕克蒂亚省曼达克尔村一座房屋的残骸，该房屋在两个月前巴基斯坦空袭中受损。 Afghan women in the village of Deh-e Kuchay, in Kandahar Province, in May 2025. 2025年5月，坎大哈省德赫库柴村的阿富汗女性。 翻译：经雷、晋其角 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site
items.content: 《纽约时报》 2026年9月11日 Jim Huylebroek for The New York Times America’s “forever war” in Afghanistan began only weeks after the Sept. 11 attacks and lasted just short of 20 years, ending in the chaos of Aug. 15, 2021, when the capital, Kabul, fell once again to the Taliban. 美国在阿富汗的“永久战争”始于9·11袭击仅数周后，持续近20年，最终在2021年8月15日的混乱中结束——首都喀布尔再次落入塔利班之手。 Journalists for The New York Times covered the war from beginning to end and have continued capturing the lives of Afghanistan’s people as they navigate a scarred landscape and an uncertain future. 《纽约时报》的记者从头到尾报道了这场战争，并继续记录阿富汗人民的生活。他们穿行于伤痕累累的土地，面对不确定的未来。 2001-2002 2001-2002 The War Begins 战争开始 Operation Enduring Freedom began on Oct. 7, 2001, with an American bombing campaign against Al Qaeda and the Taliban. American Special Operations forces teams linked up with Afghan militias opposed to the Taliban, mainly the Northern Alliance, to drive the Taliban from power. Kabul fell in mid-November, along with the Taliban stronghold of Kandahar. “持久自由行动”于2001年10月7日开始，美国对基地组织和塔利班发动轰炸。美国特种作战部队与反对塔利班的阿富汗民兵——主要是北方联盟——联手，意图将塔利班赶下台。喀布尔于11月中旬陷落，塔利班据点坎大哈也一并陷落。 In December, Osama bin Laden, Al Qaeda’s leader, escaped to Pakistan through the mountains around Tora Bora. That same month, an interim Afghan government led by Hamid Karzai was installed. 12月，基地组织领导人奥萨马·本·拉登穿过托拉博拉周边山区逃往巴基斯坦。同月，由哈米德·卡尔扎伊领导的阿富汗临时政府成立。 James Hill for The New York Times Northern Alliance troops firing on Taliban positions in rugged territory outside the northeastern city of Taloqan in October 2001. 2001年10月，北方联盟部队在东北部城市塔洛坎外围的崎岖地带向塔利班阵地开火。 Fighters for the Northern Alliance heading to the front lines near the besieged Taliban stronghold of Kunduz in November 2001. 2001年11月，北方联盟的战士前往被围困的塔利班据点昆都士附近的前线。 Tyler Hicks/The New York Times On their way into Kabul in November 2001, Northern Alliance members found a Taliban fighter in a ditch and killed him, despite his pleas. 2001年11月，北方联盟成员在进军喀布尔途中发现一名塔利班武装分子藏身沟渠，尽管对方苦苦哀求，北方联盟成员仍将其杀害。 An American B-52 bomber circling above Tora Bora in eastern Afghanistan in December 2001. 2001年12月，一架美国B-52轰炸机在阿富汗东部托拉博拉上空盘旋。 Joao Silva for The New York Times Fighters for the Eastern Alliance, another anti-Taliban militia, running for cover from Al Qaeda sniper fire in the Tora Bora mountains in December 2001. 2001年12月，另一支反塔利班民兵组织东部联盟的战士在托拉博拉山区躲避基地组织狙击手的火力。 2003-2007 2003-2007 Drift to Iraq 转向伊拉克 Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld announced an end to major combat operations in Afghanistan in May 2003. Even with a major reconstruction effort underway there, and about 8,000 American troops in place, President George W. Bush’s administration began shifting combat resources to the war in Iraq. 国防部长唐纳德·拉姆斯菲尔德于2003年5月宣布阿富汗 主要作战行动结束 。尽管那里正在进行大规模重建，并且约有8000名美军驻扎，乔治·W·布什政府已开始将作战资源转向伊拉克战争。 American soldiers from the 10th Mountain Division yelling to others to get out of the line of fire after being ambushed by Taliban fighters in southern Afghanistan in June 2006. 2006年6月，在阿富汗南部遭到塔利班战士伏击后，美国第10山地师的士兵大声呼喊其他人离开火力线。 Tyler Hicks/The New York Times Women in Kabul waiting to vote in October 2004. Afghanistan’s landmark presidential election quickly fell into dispute. 2004年10月，喀布尔的妇女排队等待投票。阿富汗具有里程碑意义的总统选举很快陷入争议。 Mohammad Akbar holding the hand of his nephew, Mohammad, age 3, at a hospital in Kandahar in May 2006. The boy was injured in an attack by U.S. forces and suffered burn injuries. 2006年5月，穆罕默德·阿克巴在坎大哈一家医院握着三岁侄子穆罕默德的手。这名男孩在美国部队的一次袭击中受伤，遭受烧伤。 Joao Silva for The New York Times British soldiers of the Royal Anglians B Company, part of NATO forces, firing toward Taliban positions after coming under attack during a patrol in Kajaki in July 2007. 2007年7月，作为北约部队一部分的英国皇家安格利亚团B连士兵在卡贾基巡逻时遭到袭击，向塔利班阵地开火。 Wounded soldiers in the Korengal Valley in eastern Afghanistan in October 2007. 2007年10月，阿富汗东部科伦加尔山谷中受伤的士兵。 Tyler Hicks/The New York Times Afghan National Army soldiers detained a man whom they believed to be a Taliban fighter during the search of a village in southern Afghanistan in May 2006. 2006年5月，阿富汗国民军士兵在阿富汗南部搜查一个村庄时，拘留了一名他们认为是塔利班战士的男子。 2008-2010 2008-2010 Recommitment and Surge 重新承诺与增兵 In February 2009, the new American president, Barack Obama, declared a recommitment to the war and deployed 17,000 more troops to Afghanistan, adding to the 36,000 already there. 2009年2月，新任美国总统贝拉克·奥巴马宣布 重新投入于这场战争 ，并 An Army patrol worked its way through the Korengal Valley in April 2009 to meet with a group of village elders. An I.E.D. exploded. Then the Taliban attacked. Soldiers scrambled. One died. 2009年4月，一支陆军巡逻队穿过科伦加尔山谷，准备与一群村中长老会面。一枚简易爆炸装置爆炸。随后塔利班发动袭击。士兵们仓皇应对。一人死亡。 Moises Saman for The New York Times A German soldier burning a flare at a campsite in the desert of Kunduz Province, in October 2009. 2009年10月，一名德国士兵在昆都士省沙漠中的一个营地点燃信号弹。 A suicide bomber struck near a hotel in Kabul in December 2009, killing at least eight people and wounding dozens. 2009年12月，一名自杀式炸弹袭击者在喀布尔一家酒店附近发动袭击，造成至少八人死亡、数十人受伤。 Moises Saman for The New York Times A bullet-pierced window at a Kabul guesthouse attacked by the Taliban in November 2009. Five United Nations workers were killed. 2009年11月，喀布尔一家宾馆遭到塔利班袭击，窗户被子弹击穿。五名联合国工作人员遇害。 Marines came under attack in Marja, in Helmand Province, in February 2010 while on their way to check a building that had been bombed earlier in the day. Most of the Marines were experiencing combat for the first time. 2010年2月，海军陆战队员在赫尔曼德省马尔贾遭到袭击，当时他们正前往检查一座当天早些时候被轰炸的建筑。大多数海军陆战队员是首次经历实战。 Moises Saman for The New York Times Village elders meeting in Marja in March 2010. 2010年3月，村中长老在马尔贾开会。 Afghan soldiers rushing a wounded police officer to an American helicopter in Kunar Province in March 2010. 2010年3月，库纳尔省，阿富汗士兵将一名受伤的警察紧急送往一架美国直升机。 Damon Winter/The New York Times American soldiers on a transport plane about to land in Mazar-i-Sharif in April 2010. 2010年4月，一架即将降落在马扎里沙里夫的运输机上的美国士兵。 An Afghan man who was detained on suspicion of being involved in an attack by militants on the first day of a national peace council meeting in Kabul in June 2010. 2010年6月，一名涉嫌参与武装分子在喀布尔全国和平委员会会议首日的袭击而被拘留的阿富汗男子。 Damon Winter/The New York Times Members of the First Battalion, 87th Infantry, tending to a wounded comrade in Kunduz in September 2010. 2010年9月，第87步兵团第一营的成员在昆都士照料一名受伤的战友。 2011-2013 2011-2013 A Troop Drawdown 部队撤减 In May 2011, a U.S. Navy SEAL team killed Osama bin Laden in a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan, where he had been living for years. In June, Mr. Obama announced that he would pull 33,000 troops from Afghanistan by mid-2012. 2011年5月，一支美国海军海豹突击队 击毙奥萨马·本·拉登 ，地点在巴基斯坦阿伯塔巴德的一处院落，他已在那里居住多年。6月，奥巴马宣布，他将在2012年中期前从阿富汗 撤出3.3万名军人 。 Soldiers boarding a transport helicopter in Kunduz in March 2011. 2011年3月，士兵们在昆都士登上一架运输直升机。 Andrea Bruce for The New York Times The mother of Khan Mohammad, a 3-month-old baby who died from exposure to the cold, being comforted before her child was washed and buried in the Nasaji Bagrami Camp for displaced persons in Kabul in February 2012. 2012年2月，在喀布尔的纳萨吉·巴格拉米流离失所者营地，三个月大的婴儿汗·穆罕默德因受寒而亡。他的母亲在为孩子清洗遗体并下葬前接受安慰。 Afghan soldiers, left, and American soldiers blew up a Taliban firing position in the village of Layadira, in Kandahar Province, in February 2013. 2013年2月，阿富汗士兵（左）和美国士兵在坎大哈省拉亚迪拉村炸毁一个塔利班射击阵地。 Sergey Ponomarev for The New York Times Members of the 101st Airborne Division in Paktia Province in April 2013. 2013年4月，第101空降师的成员在帕克蒂亚省。 Samiullah, 8 months old and malnourished, being held by his mother, Islam Bibi, 15, at a hospital in Lashkar Gah, in Helmand Province, in September 2013. 2013年9月，在赫尔曼德省拉什卡尔加一家医院，15岁的母亲伊斯兰·比比怀抱着八个月大、营养不良的萨米乌拉。 Daniel Berehulak for The New York Times Sayed Wazir, 40, a former mujahedeen, firing a rocket toward Taliban positions in Wardak Province in November 2013. 2013年11月，40岁的前圣战者赛义德·瓦齐尔在瓦尔达克省向塔利班阵地发射火箭弹。 The view from a Humvee of Highway 1, which links Kabul with Afghanistan’s other major cities, in November 2013. 2013年11月，从悍马车上眺望连接喀布尔与阿富汗其他主要城市的一号高速公路。 2014-2018 2014-2018 A Taliban Resurgence 塔利班卷土重来 On Dec. 31, 2014, the combat mission in Afghanistan formally ended , but the American military presence in the country did not. Mr. Obama announced a timetable for the withdrawal of most troops by the end of 2016. 2014年12月31日，阿富汗的战斗任务 正式结束 ，但美国在该国的军事存在并未结束。奥巴马宣布了在2016年底前撤出大部分军队的时间表。 After a 2014 election marred by fraud, Ashraf Ghani became president, but signed a power-sharing agreement with his top opponent, Abdullah Abdullah. 在2014年一场因舞弊而备受诟病的选举后，阿什拉夫·加尼成为总统，但与他的主要对手阿卜杜拉·阿卜杜拉 签署了权力分享协议 。 On the battlefield, the Afghan security forces increasingly struggled against the Taliban, taking heavy casualties and losing territory. 在战场上，阿富汗安全部队日益难以对抗塔利班，承受重大伤亡并丢失领土。 In August 2017, President Trump, early in his first term in office, said he would continue to prosecute the war . 2017年8月，特朗普总统在其第一个任期初期表示，他将 继续推进这场战争 。 Bryan Denton for The New York Times An Afghan police officer, Mohammad Qassim, 28, recovering at a hospital run by Emergency, an Italian nonprofit group, after losing his right leg to a Taliban explosive in Marja, Helmand Province. 在赫尔曼德省马尔贾，28岁的阿富汗警察穆罕默德·卡西姆在意大利非营利组织“急诊”运营的医院中康复，他因塔利班的爆炸物失去了右腿。 The aftermath of a U.S. airstrike that hit a Doctors Without Borders hospital in Kunduz in October 2015. Forty-two people were killed in the attack. 2015年10月，美国空袭击中昆都士一家无国界医生医院后的景象。42人在袭击中丧生。 Jim Huylebroek for The New York Times The bodies of 20 commandos lined up in November 2018 outside the governor’s office in Sang-e-Masha, in Ghazni Province. Their company was almost destroyed fighting the Taliban. 2018年11月，加兹尼省桑格-马沙省长办公室外，20名突击队员的遗体排成一列。他们的连队在对抗塔利班时几乎被摧毁。 A view of the outskirts of Lashkar Gah in Helmand Province in March 2016. 2016年3月，赫尔曼德省拉什卡尔加郊区的景象。 Adam Ferguson for The New York Times The Kart-e-Sakhi cemetery in Kabul in April 2016. 2016年4月，喀布尔的卡尔特萨希公墓。 2018-2020 2018-2020 A Deal With the Taliban 与塔利班达成协议 In late 2018, American and Taliban negotiators began holding peace talks in Doha, Qatar. The Afghan government was excluded from the talks; the Taliban refused to meet with its officials. 2018年底，美国和塔利班谈判代表开始在卡塔尔多哈举行和平谈判。阿富汗政府被排除在谈判之外；塔利班拒绝与其官员会面。 On Feb. 29, 2020, the United States signed a peace deal with the Taliban, opening the door to a gradual, final troop withdrawal from Afghanistan and the beginning of direct talks between the Afghan government and the Taliban to determine the country’s future. 2020年2月29日，美国与塔利班 签署和平协议 ，为从阿富汗逐步撤军打开大门，并开启阿富汗政府与塔利班之间的直接谈判，以决定该国的未来。 A funeral for one of 63 people killed at a wedding in Kabul by an Islamic State suicide bomber in August 2019. 2019年8月，一名伊斯兰国自杀式炸弹袭击者在喀布尔一场婚礼上制造爆炸，造成63人遇难，图为其中一名遇难者的葬礼。 Jim Huylebroek for The New York Times A crater left by a car-bomb attack in Kabul in September 2019. The Taliban claimed responsibility. 2019年9月，喀布尔汽车炸弹袭击留下的弹坑。塔利班声称对此负责。 Afghan police officers inspecting a replacement trench after their base was overrun by the Taliban in February 2020. 2020年2月，阿富汗警察在其基地被塔利班攻占后检查一条新建的战壕。 Jim Huylebroek for The New York Times Two children passing members of a Taliban Red Unit, an elite force, in the Alingar district of Laghman in March 2020. 2020年3月，两名儿童在拉格曼省阿林加区经过塔利班精锐部队“红色部队”成员身旁。 2021-2026 2021-2026 The Taliban’s Return 塔利班回归 On April 14, 2021, the recently sworn-in U.S. president, Joseph R. Biden Jr., called for a complete withdrawal of all American forces from Afghanistan by Sept. 11, 2021. 2021年4月14日，刚刚宣誓就职的美国总统小约瑟夫·R·拜登呼吁在2021年9月11日前从阿富汗完全撤出所有美军。 The United States had spent about $2 trillion on the war effort. About 2,400 American troops and nearly 700 troops from other nations in the coalition died. More than 40,000 civilians were killed, as well as an estimated 60,000 Afghan security forces. 美国在这场战争中花费了约2万亿美元。约2400名美军和近700名来自联军其他国家的军人死亡。超过4万名平民被杀，另有估计达6万名阿富汗安全部队人员死亡。 After the rushed withdrawal of U.S. forces, the Afghan government did not mount a significant resistance, and Taliban forces quickly regained control. Many Afghans feared a return to civil war between the Taliban and the remaining anti-Taliban fighters, but the violence affecting civilians dropped sharply with the end of the U.S. war. 在美军匆忙撤离后，阿富汗政府没有组织有效的抵抗，塔利班部队迅速重新控制局势。许多阿富汗人担心塔利班与剩余反塔利班战士之间再次爆发内战，但随着美国战争的结束，影响平民的暴力事件急剧下降。 In 2022, the Taliban government imposed a series of edicts governing every aspect of daily life, which remain in place. The rules are particularly strict for women and girls, who are no longer allowed to work at most jobs or seek formal education beyond sixth grade. 2022年，塔利班政府颁布了一系列管理日常生活各个方面的法令，这些法令仍然有效。这些规定对妇女和女孩尤其严格，她们不再被允许从事大多数工作或寻求六年级以上的正规教育。 Military conflict has not disappeared. In late 2025, Pakistan began a campaign against the armed groups operating on its border with Afghanistan, while the Taliban tighten their grip on Afghan society and defend their rule against the few remaining forces of resistance. 军事冲突并未消失。2025年底，巴基斯坦开始对在其与阿富汗边境活动的武装团体发起行动，同时塔利班收紧对阿富汗社会的控制，并抵御少数残余抵抗力量以捍卫其统治。 An American soldier aboard a Chinook helicopter as U.S. troops began their withdrawal from the country, loading up ammunition and supplies from Kandahar Airfield in May 2021. 2021年5月，美国军队开始从阿富汗撤军，一名美国士兵在坎大哈机场的一架支奴干直升机上装载弹药和补给。 Tyler Hicks/The New York Times A passenger in a car awaiting clearance at a security checkpoint in Herat in July 2021. The Taliban would soon seize Herat, the country’s third-largest city. 2021年7月，赫拉特一个安全检查站，一名车内乘客等待放行。塔利班很快将夺取该国第三大城市赫拉特。 On the day that Afghanistan’s capital, Kabul, fell to the Taliban, the group’s fighters rode a Humvee near a roundabout in the city on Aug. 15, 2021. The date is now celebrated in Afghanistan as the moment of the country’s liberation from U.S. occupation. 2021年8月15日，阿富汗首都喀布尔落入塔利班之手当天，该组织战士乘坐一辆悍马车经过城中一个环岛。这一天现在在阿富汗被视为庆祝国家从美国占领下解放的时刻。 Jim Huylebroek for The New York Times With the U.S. withdrawal deadline looming, mayhem persisted outside the Kabul airport as American Marines stood guard in August 2021. Even some Afghans holding special immigrant visas were turned away to give priority to U.S. citizens. 2021年8月，随着美国撤军期限临近，喀布尔机场外混乱持续，美国海军陆战队员站岗守卫。甚至一些持有特殊移民签证的阿富汗人也因美国优先处理本国公民而被拒之门外。 In August 2021, during the last days of the U.S. evacuation, there was another spasm of violence, when a suicide bomb exploded outside the gates of the crowded airport in Kabul. An Islamic State affiliate claimed responsibility for the attack, which killed 13 U.S. service members and scores of civilians. 2021年8月，在美国撤离的最后几天，又发生了暴力事件，一枚自杀式炸弹在拥挤的喀布尔机场门外爆炸。一个与伊斯兰国有关联的组织声称负责，袭击造成13名美国军人和数十名平民死亡。 Victor J. Blue for The New York Times Before the city fell, Khalil Haqqani appeared at a mosque in Kabul to help establish Taliban authority. When the Taliban declared an interim government, they appointed many loyalists from their rule in the 1990s, including Mr. Haqqani. 在城市陷落前，哈利勒·哈卡尼出现在喀布尔一座清真寺，帮助建立塔利班权威。当塔利班宣布临时政府时，他们任命了许多20世纪90年代统治时期的效忠者，包括哈卡尼在内。 Relatives and neighbors at the site of a U.S. drone strike that killed 10 civilians in Kabul in August 2021. 2021年8月，喀布尔一次美国无人机袭击造成10名平民死亡，图为亲属和邻居在袭击现场。 David Guttenfelder for The New York Times Children flying homemade kites on a hillside graveyard in Kabul in December 2021. The first Taliban government had banned kite flying, and Afghans feared that the pastime and other activities would be outlawed again. 2021年12月，儿童在喀布尔一个山坡坟场放自制风筝。塔利班第一届政府曾禁止放风筝，阿富汗人担心这种消遣和其他活动会再次被禁止。 A math class in a secret classroom in Afghanistan in May 2026. The Taliban banned formal education beyond sixth grade for girls. 2026年5月，阿富汗一间秘密教室里的数学课。塔利班禁止女孩接受六年级以上的正规教育。 Elise Blanchard for The New York Times Afghan women and children who had just arrived from Pakistan waiting to be registered as returnees at the Torkham border crossing in Nangarhar Province in October 2023. Seven families paid to travel with their belongings from Pakistan. 2023年10月，刚刚从巴基斯坦抵达的阿富汗妇女和儿童在楠格哈尔省托尔哈姆边境口岸等待被登记为回乡人员。七个家庭自费携带家当从巴基斯坦辗转而来。 Nasiba Ameni, 30, holding her son Abdul Hamad, 1, at a malnutrition ward in Olqan Hospital, in Daykundi Province, in December 2025. Abdul has a heart disease, and his recovery is complicated by severe malnutrition. 2025年12月，30岁的纳西巴·阿梅尼在代孔迪省奥尔坎医院营养不良病房抱着一岁的儿子阿卜杜勒·哈马德。阿卜杜勒患有心脏病，他的康复因严重营养不良而变得棘手。 Tomas Munita for The New York Times Visiting the remains of a house in August 2026 that was damaged during Pakistani airstrikes two months earlier in the village of Mandakhel, in Paktia Province. 2026年8月，探访帕克蒂亚省曼达克尔村一座房屋的残骸，该房屋在两个月前巴基斯坦空袭中受损。 Afghan women in the village of Deh-e Kuchay, in Kandahar Province, in May 2025. 2025年5月，坎大哈省德赫库柴村的阿富汗女性。 翻译：经雷、晋其角 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

items.title: 人工智能末日论：人类为何会如此担忧？
items.description: WILLIAM J. BROAD, CADE METZ2026年9月11日从大流行病到致命小行星，再到生态崩溃，人类面临诸多灭顶之灾。人工智能超智能不过是最近一个引发人们无限想象的话题。 Andrew Harnik/Associated Press It could launch a bioweapon attack, or a global drone war. It could set off a nuclear bomb. Or it could destroy human society more gradually, by hoarding all the world’s economic resources and depriving us of food, housing or medicine. 它可能发动生物武器攻击，或掀起一场全球无人机战争。它可能引爆核弹。或者，它也可能通过囤积全球所有经济资源、让我们无法获得食物、住房或药品，以一种更加渐进的方式摧毁人类社会。 These are the sorts of dark thoughts that now swirl around artificial intelligence, a technology that has already proved to be a great advance in human achievement — but that, some fear, also has the potential to snuff out humanity entirely. 这些正是如今围绕人工智能产生的一些黑暗想象。这项技术已被证明是人类成就的一项巨大进步，但一些人担心，它同样有可能让人类彻底走向灭亡。 Such anxieties made global headlines this week when an Anthropic researcher quit the industry, citing fears that his lab and others like it were building supersmart machines that humans would be unable to control. 本周，当Anthropic的一名研究人员离开这个行业，表示他担心自己所在的实验室及其他类似机构正在建造人类无法控制的超级智能机器时，这种焦虑登上了全球新闻头条。 The potential threats posed by A.I. are understandably scary. But the modern world teems with a multitude of existential risks. Humans also face the prospect of doom from killer asteroids, pandemics, thermonuclear war, climate change, giant blobs of incandescent material shot from the sun, ecological collapse and the onset of a sudden ice age. 人们对人工智能可能带来的威胁感到害怕，是可以理解的。但现代世界充斥着各种各样可能威胁人类生存的风险。人类同样面临着毁于杀手小行星、大流行病、热核战争、气候变化、太阳喷射出的巨大炽热物质团块、生态系统崩溃以及突然降临的冰河时代的可能。 The problem, scientists and public policy experts say, is not so much these threats, of which A.I. is merely the latest, but the innate human difficulty of putting them into perspective. 科学家和公共政策专家表示，问题与其说在于这些威胁本身——人工智能只是其中最新的一个，不如说在于人类天生难以正确看待和权衡这些威胁。 “We tolerate risks that we’re used to but fear the new ones,” said James K. Hammitt, the director of the Harvard Center for Risk Analysis. “我们能够容忍自己已经习惯的风险，却害怕那些新出现的风险，”哈佛大学风险分析中心主任詹姆斯·哈米特说。 We drive in cars more often than we fly in planes, he said, so “airlines are perceived as dangerous compared to motor vehicles, when they’re really not.” 他说，我们开车出行的频率高于坐飞机，所以“与机动车相比，人们会认为坐飞机更危险，但实际上并非如此”。 Artificial intelligence, he noted, “is obviously not understood and not under our perceived control, so it generates huge social concern.” 他指出，人工智能“显然还没有得到充分理解，也不在我们自认为能够控制的范围之内，因此引发了巨大的社会担忧”。 Among the tech executives and researchers building A.I. systems, there has always been a contingent that has warned of A.I.’s potential to destroy humanity. 在构建人工智能系统的科技高管和研究人员中，一直有一派人警告人工智能可能毁灭人类。 In the short term, some say, artificial intelligence could help unskilled but malicious people create viruses or toxic substances capable of causing widespread disease and death. Just on Thursday, Anthropic said it had foiled several efforts by scientists who were conducting research that potentially could lead to the development of biological weapons. 一些人认为，从短期来看，人工智能可能帮助那些缺乏专业技能但怀有恶意的人制造病毒或有毒物质，从而造成大范围的疾病和死亡。就在周四，Anthropic表示，该公司挫败了若干科学家的数次尝试；这些科学家正在进行可能导致生物武器开发的研究。 In the longer term, those warning of A.I.’s potential dangers argue that tech companies could give A.I. systems greater autonomy, connect them to the internet and even tie them into vital infrastructure, including power grids, stock markets and military weapons. Once they are connected to this infrastructure, they argue, A.I. systems could cause problems in unexpected ways. 从长期来看，那些警告人工智能潜在危险的人认为，科技公司可能赋予人工智能系统更大的自主权，将它们接入互联网，甚至让它们连接到包括电网、股市和军事武器在内的重要基础设施。他们认为，一旦与这些基础设施连接起来，人工智能系统就可能以人们意想不到的方式引发问题。 Today, when A.I. systems go rogue, companies like OpenAI can just shut them off. But some experts worry that future systems will resist efforts to shut them down. 如今，如果人工智能系统失控，OpenAI等公司只需把它们关掉即可。但一些专家担心，未来的系统可能会抵抗人类关闭它们的尝试。 For now, these are hypothetical concerns. 目前，这些都是假设性的担忧。 NASA的“小行星威胁评估项目”利用超级计算能力评估假设性小行星撞击可能造成的损害和风险。 “We are very far away,” said Oren Etzioni, a professor at the University of Washington and the founding chief executive of the Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence. “If I had to worry about either an A.I. escaping the lab and killing millions of people and a virus escaping and killing millions, it is no contest. The worry is the virus.” “我们距离那一步还非常遥远，”华盛顿大学教授、艾伦人工智能研究所创始首席执行官奥伦·埃齐奥尼说。“如果非要让我在‘人工智能逃出实验室并杀死数百万人’和‘一种病毒逃逸并杀死数百万人’这两件事之间选择一个需要担心的，我根本不会犹豫。应该担心的是病毒。” As it turns out, even anthrax has a reasonable chance at doing in humanity. 事实证明，就连炭疽也有相当的机会毁灭人类。 Anthrax has been around since ancient times, but more recently it has been a favorite of rogue nations developing biological weapons programs. 炭疽自古以来就存在，但到了近现代，它一直是发展生物武器计划的流氓国家的最爱。 Scientists have long known that a single gallon of anthrax, if suitably distributed, could end human life on earth. But that hasn’t happened, even though North Korea and other belligerent states (including Iran) have long been suspected of harboring the lethal germ. 科学家早就知道，如果将一加仑炭疽以适当的方式散播出去，就可能让地球上的人类全部死亡。但这种事情从未发生过，尽管长期以来，人们一直怀疑朝鲜以及包括伊朗在内的其他好战国家藏有这种致命病菌。 What often gets lost in the frenzied panics of modern life is that, at least with intentional threats, plain old deterrence can save the day. State actors are reluctant to unleash anthrax on an enemy because they will face retaliation — turning a strike into a suicide — thus creating an incentive for restraint. 在现代生活的疯狂恐慌中，人们经常忽略的一点是，至少对于蓄意威胁而言，最简单的威慑手段就可以避免灾难。国家行为体不愿向敌人释放炭疽，因为它们会面临报复——这会让一次攻击变成自杀式行动，从而形成了克制的动机。 The Harvard Center, founded in 1989, seeks to put these numerous doom scenarios in perspective, especially the undeterrable ones, such as environmental risks and major threats to human health. It seeks to apply decision science, economics and risk assessment to assess and improve policymaking. 成立于1989年的哈佛大学风险分析中心试图帮助人们正确看待这些形形色色的末日情景，尤其是那些无法通过威慑加以阻止的风险，例如环境风险以及人类健康的重大威胁。该中心试图运用决策科学、经济学和风险评估等方法，对政策制定进行评估并加以改进。 Similarly, NASA relies on supercomputers in its Asteroid Threat Assessment Project. Overall, the space agency puts the risk this century of an asteroid impact that would endanger human existence at essentially zero. And it calculates that earthlings can (in all likelihood) breath a sigh of relief for at least 1,000 years to come. 同样，美国国家航空航天局在“小行星威胁评估项目”中依赖超级计算机。总体而言，这家航天机构认为，本世纪发生足以威胁人类生存的小行星撞击事件的风险基本为零。该机构计算认为，地球人很可能至少在未来1000年内都可以松一口气。 And how do knowledgeable scientists assess the risk of a global pandemic that would wipe out most human life? 那么，知识渊博的科学家如何评估一场可能消灭大部分人类的全球大流行病的风险？ They peg the threat as low, if not zero. Toby Ord, a researcher at Oxford University, in his 2020 book “The Precipice: Existential Risk and the Future of Humanity,” put the 100-year risk of an existential catastrophe from a pandemic at one in 30, or roughly a 3 percent chance. 他们认为威胁很低，甚至接近于零。牛津大学研究员托比·奥德在其2020年出版的《悬崖边缘：生存性风险与人类的未来》(The Precipice: Existential Risk and the Future of Humanity)一书中估计，未来100年发生一场由大流行病引发的、足以威胁人类生存的灾难，其概率为三十分之一，也就是大约3%。 What makes the doomsayers of the tech industry different from, say, an airline scientist assessing crash risks, is that many A.I. executives and researchers held such dire beliefs even before the technology began to show its power. They believe that existential risk is a serious problem in part because they have always believed it. 科技行业那些末日论者与航空领域评估飞机失事风险的科学家不同之处在于，早在这项技术开始展现其威力之前，许多人工智能领域的高管和研究人员就已经抱有如此悲观的看法。他们之所以认为生存风险是一个严重问题，一定程度上恰恰在于他们一直以来就这么认为。 “I was there when this subculture developed,” said Zack Korman, a founder of the A.I. security company Embroidery. He was referring to his time at the University of Oxford, when it was a hotbed of the “effective altruism” movement, in which many of these fears of A.I. existential risk first incubated. Too many thinkers on the subject today, Mr. Korman said, “interpret all events in light of this story that has been told for more than a decade.” “这种亚文化形成的时候，我就在现场，”人工智能安全公司Embroidery的创始人之一扎克·科曼说。他指的是自己在牛津大学的经历。当时，那里是“有效利他主义”运动的大本营，而许多关于人工智能生存风险的担忧最初正是在这一运动中孕育出来的。科曼说，如今关于这一问题的思考者中，有太多人“用这个讲述了十多年的故事来解释所有发生的事情”。 Many of the world’s top researchers, though, do not share such beliefs. They say the fears are wildly overblown. And scientists outside Silicon Valley tend to hold a very different view about the threat of A.I. 不过，世界上许多顶尖研究人员并不认同这种看法。他们认为，这些担忧被严重夸大了。而硅谷以外的科学家往往对人工智能威胁持有截然不同的看法。 “The discussion has a frame, and it is a very particular frame. That is the frame that was there before deep learning took off, and it has stayed there,” Branton DeMoss, an A.I. researcher at Oxford, said, referring to the rise of neural networks. “And I don’t agree with it.” “这个讨论有一个既定框架，而且是一个非常特定的框架。那是深度学习兴起之前就存在的框架，并且一直沿用至今，”牛津大学人工智能研究员布兰顿·德莫斯说，他指的是神经网络的兴起。“而我并不认同这个框架。” In a recent blog post, Dr. Ord summarized the world’s different risks as moving up and down — a climate catastrophe down, a nuclear disaster up. His judgment on pandemics and A.I. is mixed: lots of changes, but no clear direction in the overall risks. 在最近的一篇贴文中，奥德博士将世界不同风险的走向概括为有升有降——气候灾难下降，核灾难上升。他对大流行病和人工智能的判断则是喜忧参半：相关情况发生了许多变化，但总体风险并没有明确的上升或下降方向。 Experts note that catastrophic and existential risks can also be mitigated with sound plans and early warning systems. Faced with a clear and present danger (like an asteroid on a collision path with the planet), humanity might well unite behind a common enemy, pushing squabbles into the background. 专家指出，灾难性风险和生存风险同样可以通过完善的应对方案和预警系统加以降低。如果面对的是一个明确而迫在眉睫的危险——比如一颗小行星正沿着撞向地球的轨道飞来——人类很可能会围绕一个共同的敌人团结起来，将纷争搁置一旁。 Dr. Ord hopes a day will come to pass for what he calls existential security. 奥德博士希望，他所称的“生存性安全”有一天能够实现。 “It is a hypothetical future state of the world where existential risk is low and kept low,” he wrote in his post. Not only would humanity extinguish the current fires, Dr. Ord wrote, but “put in place the mechanisms to ensure fire no longer poses a substantive threat.” 他在贴文中写道：“这是一种假设的未来世界状态，在这个世界里，生存风险很低，而且能够一直保持在较低水平。”奥德博士写道，人类不仅会扑灭眼下的各种火灾，还会“建立起相应的机制，确保火灾不再构成实质性的威胁”。 William J. Broad自1983年以来一直为《纽约时报》报道科学新闻。他常驻纽约。 Cade Metz撰写有关人工智能、无人驾驶汽车、机器人、虚拟现实和其他技术新兴领域的新闻。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。

BROAD, CADE METZ 2026年9月11日 从大流行病到致命小行星，再到生态崩溃，人类面临诸多灭顶之灾。人工智能超智能不过是最近一个引发人们无限想象的话题。 Andrew Harnik/Associated Press It could launch a bioweapon attack, or a global drone war. It could set off a nuclear bomb. Or it could destroy human society more gradually, by hoarding all the world’s economic resources and depriving us of food, housing or medicine. 它可能发动生物武器攻击，或掀起一场全球无人机战争。它可能引爆核弹。或者，它也可能通过囤积全球所有经济资源、让我们无法获得食物、住房或药品，以一种更加渐进的方式摧毁人类社会。 These are the sorts of dark thoughts that now swirl around artificial intelligence, a technology that has already proved to be a great advance in human achievement — but that, some fear, also has the potential to snuff out humanity entirely. 这些正是如今围绕人工智能产生的一些黑暗想象。这项技术已被证明是人类成就的一项巨大进步，但一些人担心，它同样有可能让人类彻底走向灭亡。 Such anxieties made global headlines this week when an Anthropic researcher quit the industry, citing fears that his lab and others like it were building supersmart machines that humans would be unable to control. 本周，当Anthropic的一名 研究人员离开这个行业 ，表示他担心自己所在的实验室及其他类似机构正在建造人类无法控制的超级智能机器时，这种焦虑登上了全球新闻头条。 The potential threats posed by A.I. are understandably scary. But the modern world teems with a multitude of existential risks. Humans also face the prospect of doom from killer asteroids, pandemics, thermonuclear war, climate change, giant blobs of incandescent material shot from the sun, ecological collapse and the onset of a sudden ice age. 人们对人工智能可能带来的威胁感到害怕，是可以理解的。但现代世界充斥着各种各样可能威胁人类生存的风险。人类同样面临着毁于杀手小行星、大流行病、热核战争、气候变化、太阳喷射出的巨大炽热物质团块、生态系统崩溃以及突然降临的冰河时代的可能。 The problem, scientists and public policy experts say, is not so much these threats, of which A.I. is merely the latest, but the innate human difficulty of putting them into perspective. 科学家和公共政策专家表示，问题与其说在于这些威胁本身——人工智能只是其中最新的一个，不如说在于人类天生难以正确看待和权衡这些威胁。 “We tolerate risks that we’re used to but fear the new ones,” said James K. Hammitt , the director of the Harvard Center for Risk Analysis . “我们能够容忍自己已经习惯的风险，却害怕那些新出现的风险，” 哈佛大学风险分析中心 主任 詹姆斯·哈米特 说。 We drive in cars more often than we fly in planes, he said, so “airlines are perceived as dangerous compared to motor vehicles, when they’re really not.” 他说，我们开车出行的频率高于坐飞机，所以“与机动车相比，人们会认为坐飞机更危险，但实际上并非如此”。 Artificial intelligence, he noted, “is obviously not understood and not under our perceived control, so it generates huge social concern.” 他指出，人工智能“显然还没有得到充分理解，也不在我们自认为能够控制的范围之内，因此引发了巨大的社会担忧”。 Among the tech executives and researchers building A.I. systems, there has always been a contingent that has warned of A.I.’s potential to destroy humanity. 在构建人工智能系统的科技高管和研究人员中，一直有一派人警告人工智能可能毁灭人类。 In the short term, some say, artificial intelligence could help unskilled but malicious people create viruses or toxic substances capable of causing widespread disease and death. Just on Thursday, Anthropic said it had foiled several efforts by scientists who were conducting research that potentially could lead to the development of biological weapons. 一些人认为，从短期来看，人工智能可能帮助那些缺乏专业技能但怀有恶意的人 制造病毒或有毒物质 ，从而造成大范围的疾病和死亡。就在周四，Anthropic表示，该公司挫败了若干科学家的数次尝试；这些科学家正在进行可能导致生物武器开发的研究。 In the longer term, those warning of A.I.’s potential dangers argue that tech companies could give A.I. systems greater autonomy, connect them to the internet and even tie them into vital infrastructure, including power grids, stock markets and military weapons. Once they are connected to this infrastructure, they argue, A.I. systems could cause problems in unexpected ways. 从长期来看，那些警告人工智能潜在危险的人认为，科技公司可能赋予人工智能系统更大的自主权，将它们接入互联网，甚至让它们连接到包括电网、股市和军事武器在内的重要基础设施。他们认为，一旦与这些基础设施连接起来，人工智能系统就可能以人们意想不到的方式引发问题。 Today, when A.I. systems go rogue, companies like OpenAI can just shut them off. But some experts worry that future systems will resist efforts to shut them down. 如今，如果人工智能系统失控，OpenAI等公司只需把它们关掉即可。但一些专家担心，未来的系统可能会抵抗人类关闭它们的尝试。 For now, these are hypothetical concerns. 目前，这些都是假设性的担忧。 NASA的“小行星威胁评估项目”利用超级计算能力评估假设性小行星撞击可能造成的损害和风险。 “We are very far away,” said Oren Etzioni, a professor at the University of Washington and the founding chief executive of the Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence. “If I had to worry about either an A.I. escaping the lab and killing millions of people and a virus escaping and killing millions, it is no contest. The worry is the virus.” “我们距离那一步还非常遥远，”华盛顿大学教授、艾伦人工智能研究所创始首席执行官奥伦·埃齐奥尼说。“如果非要让我在‘人工智能逃出实验室并杀死数百万人’和‘一种病毒逃逸并杀死数百万人’这两件事之间选择一个需要担心的，我根本不会犹豫。应该担心的是病毒。” As it turns out, even anthrax has a reasonable chance at doing in humanity. 事实证明，就连炭疽也有相当的机会毁灭人类。 Anthrax has been around since ancient times, but more recently it has been a favorite of rogue nations developing biological weapons programs. 炭疽自古以来就存在，但到了近现代，它一直是发展生物武器计划的流氓国家的最爱。 Scientists have long known that a single gallon of anthrax, if suitably distributed, could end human life on earth. But that hasn’t happened, even though North Korea and other belligerent states (including Iran ) have long been suspected of harboring the lethal germ. 科学家早就知道，如果将一加仑炭疽以适当的方式散播出去，就 可能让地球上的人类全部死亡 。但这种事情从未发生过，尽管长期以来，人们一直怀疑 朝鲜 以及包括 伊朗 在内的其他好战国家藏有这种致命病菌。 What often gets lost in the frenzied panics of modern life is that, at least with intentional threats, plain old deterrence can save the day. State actors are reluctant to unleash anthrax on an enemy because they will face retaliation — turning a strike into a suicide — thus creating an incentive for restraint. 在现代生活的疯狂恐慌中，人们经常忽略的一点是，至少对于蓄意威胁而言，最简单的威慑手段就可以避免灾难。国家行为体不愿向敌人释放炭疽，因为它们会面临报复——这会让一次攻击变成自杀式行动，从而形成了克制的动机。 The Harvard Center, founded in 1989, seeks to put these numerous doom scenarios in perspective, especially the undeterrable ones, such as environmental risks and major threats to human health. It seeks to apply decision science, economics and risk assessment to assess and improve policymaking. 成立于1989年的哈佛大学风险分析中心试图帮助人们正确看待这些形形色色的末日情景，尤其是那些无法通过威慑加以阻止的风险，例如环境风险以及人类健康的重大威胁。该中心试图运用决策科学、经济学和风险评估等方法，对政策制定进行评估并加以改进。 Similarly, NASA relies on supercomputers in its Asteroid Threat Assessment Project . Overall, the space agency puts the risk this century of an asteroid impact that would endanger human existence at essentially zero. And it calculates that earthlings can (in all likelihood) breath a sigh of relief for at least 1,000 years to come. 同样，美国国家航空航天局在“ 小行星威胁评估项目 ”中依赖超级计算机。总体而言，这家航天机构认为，本世纪发生足以威胁人类生存的小行星撞击事件的 风险 基本为零。该机构计算认为，地球人很可能至少在未来1000年内都可以松一口气。 And how do knowledgeable scientists assess the risk of a global pandemic that would wipe out most human life? 那么，知识渊博的科学家如何评估一场可能消灭大部分人类的全球大流行病的风险？ They peg the threat as low, if not zero. Toby Ord , a researcher at Oxford University, in his 2020 book “The Precipice: Existential Risk and the Future of Humanity,” put the 100-year risk of an existential catastrophe from a pandemic at one in 30, or roughly a 3 percent chance. 他们认为威胁很低，甚至接近于零。牛津大学研究员 托比·奥德 在其 2020年出版 的《悬崖边缘：生存性风险与人类的未来》(The Precipice: Existential Risk and the Future of Humanity)一书中估计，未来100年发生一场由大流行病引发的、足以威胁人类生存的灾难，其概率为三十分之一，也就是大约3%。 What makes the doomsayers of the tech industry different from, say, an airline scientist assessing crash risks, is that many A.I. executives and researchers held such dire beliefs even before the technology began to show its power. They believe that existential risk is a serious problem in part because they have always believed it. 科技行业那些末日论者与航空领域评估飞机失事风险的科学家不同之处在于，早在这项技术开始展现其威力之前，许多人工智能领域的高管和研究人员就已经抱有如此悲观的看法。他们之所以认为生存风险是一个严重问题，一定程度上恰恰在于他们一直以来就这么认为。 “I was there when this subculture developed,” said Zack Korman, a founder of the A.I. security company Embroidery. He was referring to his time at the University of Oxford, when it was a hotbed of the “effective altruism” movement, in which many of these fears of A.I. existential risk first incubated. Too many thinkers on the subject today, Mr. Korman said, “interpret all events in light of this story that has been told for more than a decade.” “这种亚文化形成的时候，我就在现场，”人工智能安全公司Embroidery的创始人之一扎克·科曼说。他指的是自己在牛津大学的经历。当时，那里是“有效利他主义”运动的大本营，而许多关于人工智能生存风险的担忧最初正是在这一运动中孕育出来的。科曼说，如今关于这一问题的思考者中，有太多人“用这个讲述了十多年的故事来解释所有发生的事情”。 Many of the world’s top researchers, though, do not share such beliefs. They say the fears are wildly overblown. And scientists outside Silicon Valley tend to hold a very different view about the threat of A.I. 不过，世界上许多顶尖研究人员并不认同这种看法。他们认为，这些担忧被严重夸大了。而硅谷以外的科学家往往对人工智能威胁持有截然不同的看法。 “The discussion has a frame, and it is a very particular frame. That is the frame that was there before deep learning took off, and it has stayed there,” Branton DeMoss, an A.I. researcher at Oxford, said, referring to the rise of neural networks. “And I don’t agree with it.” “这个讨论有一个既定框架，而且是一个非常特定的框架。那是深度学习兴起之前就存在的框架，并且一直沿用至今，”牛津大学人工智能研究员布兰顿·德莫斯说，他指的是神经网络的兴起。“而我并不认同这个框架。” In a recent blog post , Dr. Ord summarized the world’s different risks as moving up and down — a climate catastrophe down, a nuclear disaster up. His judgment on pandemics and A.I. is mixed: lots of changes, but no clear direction in the overall risks. 在 最近的一篇贴文 中，奥德博士将世界不同风险的走向概括为有升有降——气候灾难下降，核灾难上升。他对大流行病和人工智能的判断则是喜忧参半：相关情况发生了许多变化，但总体风险并没有明确的上升或下降方向。 Experts note that catastrophic and existential risks can also be mitigated with sound plans and early warning systems. Faced with a clear and present danger (like an asteroid on a collision path with the planet), humanity might well unite behind a common enemy, pushing squabbles into the background. 专家指出，灾难性风险和生存风险同样可以通过完善的应对方案和预警系统加以降低。如果面对的是一个明确而迫在眉睫的危险——比如一颗小行星正沿着撞向地球的轨道飞来——人类很可能会围绕一个共同的敌人团结起来，将纷争搁置一旁。 Dr. Ord hopes a day will come to pass for what he calls existential security. 奥德博士希望，他所称的“生存性安全”有一天能够实现。 “It is a hypothetical future state of the world where existential risk is low and kept low,” he wrote in his post. Not only would humanity extinguish the current fires, Dr. Ord wrote, but “put in place the mechanisms to ensure fire no longer poses a substantive threat.” 他在贴文中写道：“这是一种假设的未来世界状态，在这个世界里，生存风险很低，而且能够一直保持在较低水平。”奥德博士写道，人类不仅会扑灭眼下的各种火灾，还会“建立起相应的机制，确保火灾不再构成实质性的威胁”。 William J. Broad 自1983年以来一直为《纽约时报》报道科学新闻。他常驻纽约。 Cade Metz 撰写有关人工智能、无人驾驶汽车、机器人、虚拟现实和其他技术新兴领域的新闻。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 利用AI开发生物武器？Anthropic称阻止多起相关企图
items.description: DUSTIN VOLZ2026年9月11日Anthropic周四发布的报告列举了过去八个月其AI模型——包括聊天机器人Claude——遭到的一系列滥用情况。 Marissa Leshnov for The New York Times Anthropic said it had disrupted several potential plots this year by scientists who used its leading artificial intelligence models to conduct research that could have helped develop biological weapons. Anthropic表示，今年已多次阻止科学家利用其领先的人工智能模型开展研究的企图，这些研究可能有助于开发生物武器。 In a report describing misuses of its A.I. models, Anthropic said it could not determine whether the research served a legitimate or nefarious purpose because valid biological inquiry — the kind that can lead to breakthroughs like vaccines — can also help engineer dangerous pathogens. In the face of that uncertainty, Anthropic said it erred on the side of caution because the consequences of missing malicious activity could be severe. 在一份描述其AI模型被滥用的报告中，Anthropic表示无法确定这些研究是出于合法还是邪恶目的，因为有效的生物学研究——能带来疫苗等突破的那种——也可能有助于设计危险病原体。面对这种不确定性，Anthropic表示选择谨慎行事，因为漏掉恶意活动的后果可能很严重。 “You are not seeing someone in a comic book kind of way say, ‘Hey, I want to build a biological weapon to kill everybody,’” Jacob Klein, the head of threat intelligence at Anthropic, said in an interview. “It’s an incredibly nuanced situation.” “你不会看到有人像漫画书里那样说，‘嘿，我想制造生物武器杀死所有人，’”Anthropic威胁情报主管雅各布·克莱因在接受采访时说。“情况极其微妙。” The potential for cutting-edge A.I. models to facilitate the development of known or entirely new biological pathogens is among the gravest concerns experts have about a technology that is developing so rapidly that even its leading architects doubt whether humans will be able to fully control it. 尖端AI模型可能促进已知或全新生物病原体的开发，这是专家们对这项技术最严重的担忧之一——该技术发展如此迅速，连其领先的设计者都怀疑人类能否完全控制它。 Compared with the threat of catastrophic cyberattacks or A.I. agents that fail to align with human intentions, biological misuse has gained less attention as an existential risk of A.I., in part because past examples have generally been shown only in research settings rather than in the real world. 与灾难性网络攻击或与人类意图不一致的AI智能体相比，生物滥用作为AI的生存风险受到的关注较少，部分原因是过去的案例通常只出现在研究环境中，而非现实世界。 Andrew Weber, a senior fellow on the Council on Strategic Risks who reviewed Anthropic’s report before its release, said the findings were “chilling examples of state-sponsored biological weapons developers tapping into the rapidly advancing capabilities” of leading A.I. models. 战略风险委员会高级研究员安德鲁·韦伯在报告发布前审阅了Anthropic的报告。他说，这些发现是“国家支持的生物武器开发者利用领先AI模型快速进步能力的案例，令人不寒而栗”。 The lengthy report that Anthropic published on Thursday cataloged a litany of misuses on various models of its Claude A.I. chatbot over the past eight months. Some examples were similar to past disclosures from Anthropic and other A.I. labs, including suspected Chinese and Iranian government-linked actors targeting dissident and diaspora communities for surveillance. Anthropic周四发布的长篇报告列举了过去八个月其Claude聊天机器人各模型被滥用的一系列事例。一些例子与Anthropic和其他AI实验室过去的披露类似，包括疑似与中国和伊朗政府有关联的行为者针对异见者和侨民社区进行监视。 The report also highlighted cases of Russian state media using Claude to generate online propaganda masquerading as independent reporting, including fabricated claims about an election in Moldova. 报告还提到俄罗斯官方媒体使用Claude生成伪装成独立报道的在线宣传，包括关于摩尔多瓦选举的捏造内容。 Anthropic documented another genre of abuse it said was new: attempts to use Claude to develop software for conventional weapons design and development, including firearms, missiles, armed drones and bombs. It detailed three cases in China, two in Russia and one in Yemen. Anthropic记录了另一种它认为属于新型的滥用：试图利用Claude开发用于常规武器设计和开发的软件，包括枪支、导弹、武装无人机和炸弹。报告详细描述了在中国的三起、俄罗斯的两起和也门的一起案例。 The report does not identify by name which parties were involved in the Yemeni case, but the context makes clear that it is referring to the Iran-backed Houthi militia. A.I. use by terrorist networks is a growing concern among U.S. security officials. 报告未点名也门这一例涉及哪一方，但上下文清楚表明指的是伊朗支持的胡塞武装。恐怖网络使用AI正日益成为美国安全官员的担忧。 But among all the categories of threats shared in the report, none may be as worrisome as the biological research cases. Anthropic did not disclose the names of researchers or institutions that it blocked, their countries of affiliation or the specific biological agents at issue, in part because of its uncertainty about their aims. 但在报告列出的所有威胁类别中，可能生物研究最令人担忧。Anthropic未披露它阻止的研究人员或机构的名称、所属国家或所涉具体生物制剂，部分原因是其不确定这些人的目的。 Still, Anthropic said the scientists circumvented its controls intended to prevent users from blocked regions from gaining access to its A.I. models and worked to “obfuscate the purpose of their research to evade our safeguards.” The company banned accounts associated with the research. 尽管如此，Anthropic表示，这些科学家规避了旨在阻止被封锁地区用户访问其AI模型的控制措施，并设法“混淆研究目的以避开我们的安全护栏”。该公司封禁了相关账户。 In one example from May, a scientist sought Claude’s help with writing a grant application for funding to conduct research intended to experiment on the chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne malady that can lead to months of severe pain and other symptoms. Such research, known as gain of function, can be legitimate and lead to vaccine development, but it can also create superbug versions of viruses. In this instance, the scientist wanted to engineer mutations to the virus that would make it more harmful as it repeatedly infected live animals. 在5月的一个案例中，一名科学家寻求Claude帮助撰写拨款申请，以资助针对基孔肯雅病毒的研究。这是一种蚊媒疾病，可导致数月严重疼痛和其他症状。这类研究被称为功能获得性研究，可能合法且促成疫苗开发，但也可能制造出超级病毒。在此例中，科学家想要设计病毒突变，使其在反复感染活体动物时更具危害性。 Anthropic said it believed the particular research was worrisome in part because it could discern that the work was intended to be performed at a military research institute. Anthropic表示，它认为这项研究令人担忧，部分原因是它能够辨别出这项工作拟在一家军事研究机构进行。 “What we don’t know is if the research was meant to be weaponized,” Mr. Klein said. “But a military institution doing gain-of-function research is concerning.” “我们不知道的是，这项研究是否有武器化意图，”克莱因说。“但军事机构进行功能获得性研究令人担忧。” Anthropic said evaluations from last year of its older models demonstrated that they were not yet able to meaningfully assist in conducting dangerous biological research. Its current models are more able to complete complex scientific research, the company said, which spurred tighter safeguards intended to restrict access to a wide range of dual-use biological research queries. Anthropic表示，去年对其旧模型的评估表明，它们尚不能有效协助进行危险的生物研究。该公司称，当前模型更有能力完成复杂科学研究，这促使其收紧了安全护栏，以限制多种两用生物研究的提问。 Susan Monarez, a microbiologist and public health expert who oversaw a review of national biosecurity preparedness in the Obama administration, also reviewed the Anthropic report before its publication. She said the findings provided real-world evidence to support concerns that bad actors were trying to covertly use advanced A.I. “to improve their chances of building biological pathogens that could cause significant harm.” 微生物学家兼公共卫生专家苏珊·莫纳雷斯曾在奥巴马政府负责监督国家生物安全准备工作的审查，她也在报告发布前审阅了Anthropic的报告。她说，这些发现提供了现实证据，支持了有关不良行为者正试图秘密利用先进AI的担忧，这些行为者试图“提高其制造可能造成重大伤害的生物病原体的机会”。 Dr. Monarez, who briefly served as the director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention last year, said A.I. held enormous promise to usher in an era of medical breakthroughs that save and extend lives. But the same abilities that make that possible, she added, could also “let bad actors hide in plain sight, using seemingly legitimate research to create pathogens we may not see coming and may not be able to stop once released.” 去年曾短暂担任美国疾病控制与预防中心主任的莫纳雷斯说，AI有着巨大前景，可开启一个拯救和延长生命的医学突破时代。但她补充说，使其成为可能的同样能力也可能“让不良行为者在光天化日之下，利用看似合法的研究制造我们可能无法预见、一旦释放可能无法阻止的病原体”。 Mr. Weber of the Council on Strategic Risks, who also served as the assistant secretary of defense for nuclear, chemical and biological defense programs during the Obama administration, called for limiting access to A.I. tools capable of this level of biological research to trusted researchers only. 战略风险委员会的韦伯也曾在奥巴马政府担任负责核、化学和生物防御项目的助理国防部长。他呼吁将能够进行这种级别生物研究的AI工具仅限于可信研究人员使用。 “The fact that Russia, China and North Korea continue to develop prohibited biological weapons makes it imperative that we deny their researchers access to these extraordinarily capable models,” he said. “俄罗斯、中国和朝鲜继续开发被禁止的生物武器，这使我们必须阻止其研究人员使用这些极其强大的模型，”他说。 Dustin Volz为时报撰写网络安全和情报方面的文章，他常驻华盛顿。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。
items.content: DUSTIN VOLZ 2026年9月11日 Anthropic周四发布的报告列举了过去八个月其AI模型——包括聊天机器人Claude——遭到的一系列滥用情况。 Marissa Leshnov for The New York Times Anthropic said it had disrupted several potential plots this year by scientists who used its leading artificial intelligence models to conduct research that could have helped develop biological weapons. Anthropic表示，今年已多次阻止科学家利用其领先的人工智能模型开展研究的企图，这些研究可能有助于开发生物武器。 In a report describing misuses of its A.I. models, Anthropic said it could not determine whether the research served a legitimate or nefarious purpose because valid biological inquiry — the kind that can lead to breakthroughs like vaccines — can also help engineer dangerous pathogens. In the face of that uncertainty, Anthropic said it erred on the side of caution because the consequences of missing malicious activity could be severe. 在一份描述其AI模型被滥用的报告中，Anthropic表示无法确定这些研究是出于合法还是邪恶目的，因为有效的生物学研究——能带来疫苗等突破的那种——也可能有助于设计危险病原体。面对这种不确定性，Anthropic表示选择谨慎行事，因为漏掉恶意活动的后果可能很严重。 “You are not seeing someone in a comic book kind of way say, ‘Hey, I want to build a biological weapon to kill everybody,’” Jacob Klein, the head of threat intelligence at Anthropic, said in an interview. “It’s an incredibly nuanced situation.” “你不会看到有人像漫画书里那样说，‘嘿，我想制造生物武器杀死所有人，’”Anthropic威胁情报主管雅各布·克莱因在接受采访时说。“情况极其微妙。” The potential for cutting-edge A.I. models to facilitate the development of known or entirely new biological pathogens is among the gravest concerns experts have about a technology that is developing so rapidly that even its leading architects doubt whether humans will be able to fully control it. 尖端AI模型可能促进已知或全新生物病原体的开发，这是专家们对这项技术最严重的担忧之一——该技术发展如此迅速，连其领先的设计者都怀疑人类能否完全控制它。 Compared with the threat of catastrophic cyberattacks or A.I. agents that fail to align with human intentions , biological misuse has gained less attention as an existential risk of A.I., in part because past examples have generally been shown only in research settings rather than in the real world. 与 灾难性网络攻击 或 与人类意图不一致 的AI智能体相比，生物滥用作为AI的生存风险受到的关注较少，部分原因是过去的案例通常只出现在 研究环境 中，而非现实世界。 Andrew Weber, a senior fellow on the Council on Strategic Risks who reviewed Anthropic’s report before its release, said the findings were “chilling examples of state-sponsored biological weapons developers tapping into the rapidly advancing capabilities” of leading A.I. models. 战略风险委员会高级研究员安德鲁·韦伯在报告发布前审阅了Anthropic的报告。他说，这些发现是“国家支持的生物武器开发者利用领先AI模型快速进步能力的案例，令人不寒而栗”。 The lengthy report that Anthropic published on Thursday cataloged a litany of misuses on various models of its Claude A.I. chatbot over the past eight months. Some examples were similar to past disclosures from Anthropic and other A.I. labs, including suspected Chinese and Iranian government-linked actors targeting dissident and diaspora communities for surveillance. Anthropic周四发布的 长篇报告 列举了过去八个月其Claude聊天机器人各模型被滥用的一系列事例。一些例子与Anthropic和其他AI实验室过去的披露类似，包括疑似与中国和伊朗政府有关联的行为者针对异见者和侨民社区进行监视。 The report also highlighted cases of Russian state media using Claude to generate online propaganda masquerading as independent reporting, including fabricated claims about an election in Moldova. 报告还提到俄罗斯官方媒体使用Claude生成伪装成独立报道的在线宣传，包括关于摩尔多瓦选举的捏造内容。 Anthropic documented another genre of abuse it said was new: attempts to use Claude to develop software for conventional weapons design and development, including firearms, missiles, armed drones and bombs. It detailed three cases in China, two in Russia and one in Yemen. Anthropic记录了另一种它认为属于新型的滥用：试图利用Claude开发用于常规武器设计和开发的软件，包括枪支、导弹、武装无人机和炸弹。报告详细描述了在中国的三起、俄罗斯的两起和也门的一起案例。 The report does not identify by name which parties were involved in the Yemeni case, but the context makes clear that it is referring to the Iran-backed Houthi militia. A.I. use by terrorist networks is a growing concern among U.S. security officials. 报告未点名也门这一例涉及哪一方，但上下文清楚表明指的是伊朗支持的胡塞武装。 恐怖网络使用AI 正日益成为美国安全官员的担忧。 But among all the categories of threats shared in the report, none may be as worrisome as the biological research cases. Anthropic did not disclose the names of researchers or institutions that it blocked, their countries of affiliation or the specific biological agents at issue, in part because of its uncertainty about their aims. 但在报告列出的所有威胁类别中，可能生物研究最令人担忧。Anthropic未披露它阻止的研究人员或机构的名称、所属国家或所涉具体生物制剂，部分原因是其不确定这些人的目的。 Still, Anthropic said the scientists circumvented its controls intended to prevent users from blocked regions from gaining access to its A.I. models and worked to “obfuscate the purpose of their research to evade our safeguards.” The company banned accounts associated with the research. 尽管如此，Anthropic表示，这些科学家规避了旨在阻止被封锁地区用户访问其AI模型的控制措施，并设法“混淆研究目的以避开我们的安全护栏”。该公司封禁了相关账户。 In one example from May, a scientist sought Claude’s help with writing a grant application for funding to conduct research intended to experiment on the chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne malady that can lead to months of severe pain and other symptoms. Such research, known as gain of function, can be legitimate and lead to vaccine development, but it can also create superbug versions of viruses. In this instance, the scientist wanted to engineer mutations to the virus that would make it more harmful as it repeatedly infected live animals. 在5月的一个案例中，一名科学家寻求Claude帮助撰写拨款申请，以资助针对基孔肯雅病毒的研究。这是一种蚊媒疾病，可导致数月严重疼痛和其他症状。这类研究被称为功能获得性研究，可能合法且促成疫苗开发，但也可能制造出超级病毒。在此例中，科学家想要设计病毒突变，使其在反复感染活体动物时更具危害性。 Anthropic said it believed the particular research was worrisome in part because it could discern that the work was intended to be performed at a military research institute. Anthropic表示，它认为这项研究令人担忧，部分原因是它能够辨别出这项工作拟在一家军事研究机构进行。 “What we don’t know is if the research was meant to be weaponized,” Mr. Klein said. “But a military institution doing gain-of-function research is concerning.” “我们不知道的是，这项研究是否有武器化意图，”克莱因说。“但军事机构进行功能获得性研究令人担忧。” Anthropic said evaluations from last year of its older models demonstrated that they were not yet able to meaningfully assist in conducting dangerous biological research. Its current models are more able to complete complex scientific research, the company said, which spurred tighter safeguards intended to restrict access to a wide range of dual-use biological research queries. Anthropic表示，去年对其旧模型的评估表明，它们尚不能有效协助进行危险的生物研究。该公司称，当前模型更有能力完成复杂科学研究，这促使其收紧了安全护栏，以限制多种两用生物研究的提问。 Susan Monarez, a microbiologist and public health expert who oversaw a review of national biosecurity preparedness in the Obama administration, also reviewed the Anthropic report before its publication. She said the findings provided real-world evidence to support concerns that bad actors were trying to covertly use advanced A.I. “to improve their chances of building biological pathogens that could cause significant harm.” 微生物学家兼公共卫生专家苏珊·莫纳雷斯曾在奥巴马政府负责监督国家生物安全准备工作的审查，她也在报告发布前审阅了Anthropic的报告。她说，这些发现提供了现实证据，支持了有关不良行为者正试图秘密利用先进AI的担忧，这些行为者试图“提高其制造可能造成重大伤害的生物病原体的机会”。 Dr. Monarez, who briefly served as the director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention last year, said A.I. held enormous promise to usher in an era of medical breakthroughs that save and extend lives. But the same abilities that make that possible, she added, could also “let bad actors hide in plain sight, using seemingly legitimate research to create pathogens we may not see coming and may not be able to stop once released.” 去年曾短暂担任美国疾病控制与预防中心主任的莫纳雷斯说，AI有着巨大前景，可开启一个拯救和延长生命的医学突破时代。但她补充说，使其成为可能的同样能力也可能“让不良行为者在光天化日之下，利用看似合法的研究制造我们可能无法预见、一旦释放可能无法阻止的病原体”。 Mr. Weber of the Council on Strategic Risks, who also served as the assistant secretary of defense for nuclear, chemical and biological defense programs during the Obama administration, called for limiting access to A.I. tools capable of this level of biological research to trusted researchers only. 战略风险委员会的韦伯也曾在奥巴马政府担任负责核、化学和生物防御项目的助理国防部长。他呼吁将能够进行这种级别生物研究的AI工具仅限于可信研究人员使用。 “The fact that Russia, China and North Korea continue to develop prohibited biological weapons makes it imperative that we deny their researchers access to these extraordinarily capable models,” he said. “俄罗斯、中国和朝鲜继续开发被禁止的生物武器，这使我们必须阻止其研究人员使用这些极其强大的模型，”他说。 Dustin Volz 为时报撰写网络安全和情报方面的文章，他常驻华盛顿。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 青岛造船厂内外籍货船起火，25人遇难
items.description: BERRY WANG, ALI WATKINS2026年9月11日周四，一艘货轮在中国青岛靠港时起火，消防车停靠在该货轮附近，图片由中国官方媒体发布。 Li Aoqiu/Xinhua, via Associated Press Twenty-five people were killed on Thursday after a fire broke out on a cargo ship that was docked in Qingdao, China, state media outlets reported. 据官方媒体报道，周四，一艘停靠在中国青岛的货船发生火灾，造成25人遇难。 The fire broke out at around 11:15 a.m. local time on a foreign-flagged ship that was undergoing maintenance, according to CCTV, China’s state broadcaster. The vessel was docked in a shipyard owned by Qingdao Beihai Shipbuilding, a subsidiary of a state-owned conglomerate. 据中国国家广播电视台中央电视台报道，火灾发生在当地时间上午11点15分左右，起火的是一艘正在接受维修的外籍货船。该船停靠在一家国有企业集团的子公司青岛北海造船公司所属的造船厂内。 Qingdao, in Shandong Province in eastern China, is a high-volume trade hub that has one of the busiest ports in the world and is also home to one of the country’s most strategically important naval bases. 青岛位于中国东部的山东省，是一个吞吐量巨大的贸易枢纽，拥有世界上最繁忙的港口之一，也是中国最具战略意义的海军基地之一的所在地。 The ship had 42 people onboard at the time of the blaze, which was extinguished several hours later and whose cause remained unclear. Twelve people were safely evacuated and five injured people were taken to hospital where they were in a stable condition, according to state media. 火灾发生时船上共有42人。大火在几小时后被扑灭，起因尚不清楚。据官方媒体报道，有12人安全撤出，五人受伤送医，目前情况稳定。 The fire prompted a large-scale emergency response at the shipyard. China’s leader, Xi Jinping, has called for a prompt investigation into its cause. 这场大火在造船厂引发了大规模的紧急响应。中国领导人习近平已要求对起火原因展开迅速调查。 Chinese state media identified the vessel as the Ocean Melody. According to Marine Traffic, a ship tracking platform, a Liberian-flagged vessel with the same name had been docked in Qingdao for at least 10 days. 中国官方媒体确认这艘船名为“海洋旋律”号。根据船舶跟踪平台Marine Traffic的数据，一艘同名的利比里亚籍船只已在青岛停靠了至少10天。 Berry Wang是《纽约时报》记者/研究员，常驻香港。 Ali Watkins为《纽约时报》报道国际新闻，她常驻贝尔法斯特。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
